newsitem.title: UK: Union calls for clarity in U.K. oil refining plans.
newsitem.headline: Union calls for clarity in U.K. oil refining plans.

text.p: A trade union spokesman on Friday called on oil companies to quell speculation that a restructuring move was imminent in Britain's Milford Haven oil refining complex.

Danny Fellowes, district spokesman for the Transport and General Workers Union, said up to 1,000 jobs could be lost if Chevron Corp closed its 112,000 barrels per day (bpd) Gulf refinery or if Gulf merged with another operator in the area.
He called on the company to put employees' minds at rest: "We've been getting rumours and speculation, but this one has taken off and it is in everyone's interest if the refineries confirm or deny."

Fellowes cited mounting speculation among workers that the Gulf refinery in south Wales would close or that it would merge with the 108,000 bpd Elf Aquitaine /Murphy Oil Corp plant located nearby. Texaco also owns a 180,000 bpd plant in the area.
A Gulf Oil spokesman said: "We have a policy of not commenting on any negotiations that may or may not be going on."
Elf, Murco and Texaco officials were not available for comment, but an industry source familiar with the refineries said he expected an announcement within 10 days.
Industry analysts have been expecting a reduction in Britain's 1.8 million bpd refining capacity because of overcapacity and weak margins.
Fellowes said Pembrokeshire's three refineries made it the most likely area to suffer in any cutback.
